title: Converge node-provisioning interfaces and deprecate legacy leasepool service
creator: Maya Gupta
description: Refactor the GPU fleet node-provisioning surface to unify multiple provisioner implementations, remove the legacy leasepool service, and simplify the capacity planner's reconciliation loop. This ticket covers interface consolidation, a migration adapter for backward compatibility, dependency upgrades (controller-runtime, client-go), and an incremental canary rollout to avoid service disruption.
background: Over the past three years we accumulated two provisioner implementations (legacy leasepool + new allocator) and multiple ad-hoc reconciliation paths in the capacity planner. This has led to duplicated state transitions, race conditions during node handoff, and high tail latencies when scaling up for burst workloads. Several incidents (see postmortems linked below) traced back to leasepool <> allocator handshakes and stale leases that caused transient capacity loss.
proposed_solution: 1) Extract a minimal Provisioner interface that all consumers use for creating, annotating, and releasing nodes. 2) Implement an adapter layer that routes calls to either the new allocator or the legacy leasepool while feature-flagging the adapter. 3) Succinctly centralize lifecycle transitions in the fleet controller state machine and remove duplicate reconciliation paths inside the capacity planner. 4) Upgrade controller-runtime from v0.12 -> v0.15 and client-go from 1.23 -> 1.27 to get stable leader-election and backoff primitives. 5) Add comprehensive unit and integration tests and run a staged canary.
migration_steps: Audit all consumers of node-provision APIs and add feature-flagged calls to new Provisioner interface
Implement adapter that forwards to legacy leasepool when feature flag is off
Run e2e tests in pre-prod with adapter-on and populate synthetic load profiles
Flip feature flag in canary region A (us-west-2) for 10% of autoscaler traffic
Monitor metrics for 48h, rollback if failed_provision_rate > 1% or median_provision_time regresses > 20%
After canary success, turn off legacy leasepool path and remove code in small PRs
Run rolling upgrade across regions and mark runtime-2.4 release
acceptance_criteria: All node provisioning and release flows use the new Provisioner interface or adapter
Legacy leasepool code is behind a feature flag and can be turned off without loss of capacity
Unit test coverage for provisioner adapters >= 85% and integration test suite passes on CI
Provisioning median latency reduced by at least 10% under burst load compared to baseline
Canary run of 48h in us-west-2 with <1% failure for provision requests and no customer incidents
No increase in evicted workload rate during rollout
risks: Unexpected interactions with older Dedicated clusters that assume leasepool annotations
Controller-runtime upgrade may change leader-election semantics causing brief controller dupes
Race conditions if consumers bypass adapter and call internals (audit needed)
Rollback complexity if adapter removal happens too early
tests: Unit tests for Provisioner interface and both adapter branches
Integration tests: create/evict/replace node scenarios with synthetic KV cache loads
Load test: step-increase GPU requests to measure provision latency and tail behavior
Chaos test: simulate node registration delays and API server flaps during reconciliation
